reasoning: The December 2020 meeting introduced explicit outcome-based forward guidance tying asset purchases to 'substantial further progress' toward maximum employment and price stability goals, replacing the prior vague 'at least at the current pace' language. Additionally, the directive was upgraded from an open-ended pace commitment to specific quantified monthly floors ($80 billion Treasuries, $40 billion MBS), transforming QE from a market-functioning backstop into a goal-linked accommodation tool with a defined threshold for tapering. This constitutes the introduction of a new QE framework with explicit exit criteria, analogous to the 2012 QE3 outcome-based structure.
key_quote: the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals
